solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique after crossings); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Large area, no doubt — maybe Asia, some suggest initially

definitions.text: Large area, no doubt — maybe Asia, some suggest initially

indicators.note: initially asks for the opening letter of each of the eight words before it

explanation.surface: Someone argues that a vast region, Asia perhaps, is certainly big.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and the definition: the first letters spell the answer, and the sentence itself describes a continent-sized expanse.
explanation.definitionFit: A continent such as Asia is a huge expanse of land, a large area beyond question.

clue.text: Fuss about vocab omitting British fruit

indicators.note: about means the word for fuss goes around the trimmed vocab

parts.note: ado is fuss or bother

indicators.note: omitting says the letter standing for British is dropped from vocab

explanation.surface: Someone grumbles about vocabulary, then the clue swerves into a piece of fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'omitting British' drops the B from vocab; 'about' puts the word for fuss around what remains, split either side.
explanation.definitionFit: The green pear-shaped produce of a tropical tree is botanically a fruit.

clue.text: Daughter with Yankee beau

parts.note: and means together with
Yankee is the NATO phonetic alphabet word for Y

explanation.surface: A daughter turns up with her American boyfriend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beau' here is the older sense of a fashionable, well-dressed man, not a boyfriend.
explanation.definitionFit: A beau in the old sense is a fop, a man devoted to smart clothes.

clue.text: Skill at crossing river

indicators.note: crossing means the word at stretches across and so surrounds the river letter

explanation.surface: Someone is adept at getting over a river.
explanation.definitionFit: Craft or technique, as in the art of conversation, is a synonym for skill.

clue.text: Test racer smashed vehicle!

indicators.note: smashed means the letters of test racer are broken up and rebuilt

explanation.surface: A racing car on a test run is wrecked.
explanation.definitionFit: A tram running on rails in American streets is a passenger vehicle.

clue.text: Got up to display national emblem

definitions.meaning: past tense of rising from bed or a seat
the flower that serves as England's emblem

explanation.surface: Someone stood up to show off their country's symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: Stood up is the past of arise, and the red flower is England's national symbol.

clue.text: Welcome referring to Church the writer's supporting

indicators.note: in a down answer the supporting piece sits underneath the others

parts.note: re means concerning or referring to
CE is the Church of England
the writer refers to the setter, so the writer's (writer has) becomes I've

explanation.surface: A greeting about the church is something the author endorses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the writer's' is read as 'the writer has', I'VE; 'supporting' puts it at the bottom of this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: To welcome guests is to greet and take them in, a sense of accepting visitors.

clue.text: Country health resort, fashionable

parts.note: a spa is a resort with mineral springs
in means in fashion

explanation.surface: A trendy rural wellness retreat is being described.
explanation.definitionFit: The Iberian kingdom with Madrid as capital is a European nation.

clue.text: Time of day to return unchanged

definitions.text: Time of day to return unchanged

indicators.note: says the word for that hour reads the same when turned back to front

parts.note: midday, twelve o'clock

explanation.surface: It is the hour at which something comes back exactly as it left.
explanation.walkthrough: The midday word is a palindrome, so 'to return unchanged' describes it read backwards as well as forwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Twelve o'clock midday is a particular hour.

clue.text: Renegade can't tour after review

indicators.note: after review means the letters of can't tour are looked over and rearranged

explanation.surface: A rebel band is banned from touring once officials reassess them.
explanation.definitionFit: A traitor who switches sides is a deserter, a renegade.

clue.text: Sweetheart's lively valley do

indicators.note: lively signals the letters of valley do are set dancing into a new order

explanation.surface: A sweetheart's party in the valley is a cheerful one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'do' is a party in the surface but simply two letters of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: An old-fashioned term for a woman someone is in love with, a beloved.

clue.text: Be out longer than intended having finished taking skins up

parts.note: over means ended or finished

indicators.note: in a down answer up means the word for skins is read from the bottom

parts.note: peels are fruit skins

explanation.surface: Someone finished stripping hides and stayed out too long.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses PEELS to SLEEP in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Being out cold in slumber past the alarm is staying asleep too long.

clue.text: Recalling a number one island

indicators.note: recalling, calling back, means the pieces are read in reverse

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone remembers an island that ranked first.
explanation.definitionFit: A small Hebridean isle off Mull, famous for Saint Columba's abbey.

clue.text: Pair, ignoring me, come up with article in French

indicators.note: ignoring says the letters of me are left out of come up

parts.note: le is the French masculine definite article

explanation.surface: A couple, snubbing the speaker, show up with a piece written in French.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ignoring me' strips ME from COME UP to leave COUP.
explanation.definitionFit: Two people or things together make a twosome.

clue.text: Dad's Army, right for Elvis, say?

parts.note: pop is a name for dad, so dad's is pop's
TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve

explanation.surface: It evokes the TV sitcom Dad's Army, with someone right for an Elvis role.
explanation.walkthrough: Dad's Army is a classic British TV comedy about the Home Guard; TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve.
explanation.definitionFit: Elvis Presley is an example of a famous chart singer; 'say' marks the example.

clue.text: Credit facility line

parts.note: CR is the accounting abbreviation for credit
facility means ease, as in doing something with facility

explanation.surface: A bank offers a credit facility line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'facility' in the surface is a banking product, but here it means effortlessness.
explanation.definitionFit: A fold mark pressed into cloth or paper is a line.

clue.text: Like Great Bear, some mariners tell a rookie

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Seasoned sailors teach a novice about the constellation they steer by.
explanation.definitionFit: The Great Bear is a constellation, so it is of the stars.

clue.text: End street work

parts.note: OP, short for opus, is a work

explanation.surface: Someone calls a halt to roadworks.
explanation.definitionFit: To halt or cease something is to bring it to an end.

clue.text: Maybe past worrying

definitions.meaning: the past is one grammatical time form of a verb, as are present and future

explanation.surface: Something possibly behind us is troubling.
explanation.definitionFit: Grammar's past is one verb time form, and someone anxious is on edge.

clue.text: Highlights importance of introduction of safety locks

indicators.note: introduction of asks for the opening letter of safety

parts.note: tresses are long locks of hair

explanation.surface: Someone emphasises how vital it is to bring in security locks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'locks' looks like door fittings but means hair.
explanation.definitionFit: To emphasise or underline the significance of something is to put weight on it.

clue.text: Second trite idea leading to derision

parts.note: corn is hackneyed, sentimental material

explanation.surface: A second stale notion earns mockery.
explanation.definitionFit: Contempt and mockery are what derision expresses.

clue.text: Something loathed in gymkhana, the mare?

indicators.note: in says the answer sits within the following words, spanning them

explanation.surface: At a horse show someone wonders whether the mare is the hated one.
explanation.walkthrough: A gymkhana is a British horse-riding event for young riders.
explanation.definitionFit: A thing or person detested, cursed or abhorred is a curse word for it.

clue.text: Commercial securing India's support

indicators.note: securing means the advert holds the India letter inside it

parts.note: an ad is a commercial
India is the NATO phonetic alphabet word for I; the answer's letters sitting backwards in the word India's is a coincidence

explanation.surface: An advert backing India's cause is described.
explanation.definitionFit: Help or assistance given is support.

clue.text: Forgo leer every so often — this one?

definitions.text: Forgo leer every so often — this one?

indicators.note: every so often picks alternate letters, here the second, fourth and so on

explanation.surface: Avoid occasional leering, especially the kind meant here.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines too: 'this one?' points to the kind of leering look being forgone.
explanation.definitionFit: A lecherous stare is a leer, the very look the clue tells us to give up.

clue.text: Sadly it may fall — hurry!

definitions.meaning: a drop of water shed from the eye when crying

explanation.surface: Something may come down regretfully, so get a move on.
explanation.walkthrough: The two senses are pronounced differently: one rhymes with 'fear', the other with 'fair'.
explanation.definitionFit: A drop shed in weeping, and to race along at speed, are the two senses.

clue.text: Nit-picking editor briefly in small room off kitchen?

indicators.note: in means the editor letters go inside the storeroom word

parts.note: a pantry is a small storeroom off a kitchen
ED is the short form of editor

explanation.surface: A fussy editor is squeezed into a tiny room beside the kitchen.
explanation.definitionFit: Excessive concern with minor details and petty rules is fussy hair-splitting.
